Welcome to the documentation for the **Colorado Pollen Detection** project. This pipeline is designed to handle high-resolution `.czi` (Zeiss) microscopy scans, segment individual pollen grains, and classify them by species using state-of-the-art **YOLOv8 Instance Segmentation** architectures.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Segmentation-Based**: All labeling in this project is performed as **Instance Segmentation** (polygons), not just bounding boxes. We utilize the enormous 40M parameter `yolov8l-seg.pt` model to trace exact, mathematically precise masks around pollen perimeters.

## 🚀 Key Features

- **High-Resolution Tiling**: Effortlessly process scans larger than 20,000 pixels by decomposing them into manageable training tiles.
- **Max-Z Projection**: Automated MIP reduction to consolidate focus levels without losing detail.
- **Rigorous 80/10/10 Split**: The pipeline enforces a strictly isolated 10% Test dataset, guaranteeing totally unbiased post-training evaluation metrics.
- **Automated Negative Filtering**: 100% automated ingestion of purely empty background images to hyper-penalize false-positive debris detections.

## 📦 Data Storage Policy

To keep the repository lightweight and efficient, large datasets and model weights are **not** stored on GitHub. Instead, they are synchronized with the **CESNET S3 (S3.cl4.du.cesnet.cz)** storage.

- **Source Scans**: Stored in `s3://bucket/PEG/Colorado/detect_images/`
- **YOLO Datasets**: Stored dynamically via `s3://bucket/PEG/Colorado/Staged_area/` and `s3://bucket/PEG/Colorado/Staged_negatives/`
- **Models**: Stored reliably in `s3://bucket/PEG/Colorado/trained_models/`

## 🏷️ Roboflow Annotation

While the pipeline relies heavily on high-throughput automated slicing and `pseudo_label.py` scripts natively, the human-in-the-loop manual curation for the base general pollen model is hosted externally. You can review, correct, and track the instance-segmentation polygon masks online:

**[Roboflow: Pollen Lazy Labeling](https://app.roboflow.com/charles-university/pollen_lazy_labeling/7)**

## 📖 Get Started

Check the following sections to get up and running:

- [Ingestion Tutorial](tutorials/ingestion.qmd): How to convert your first .czi folder.
- **Training**: Set up GPU training using `src/train_pollen.py`.
- **Pseudo-Labeling**: Auto-annotate tiles using `src/pseudo_label.py`.
